question: Which high priest of the return am I?
reference: Ezra 3; Haggai 1; Zechariah 3 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Joshua No. 4')

clues: I served as high priest when the exiles came back from Babylon.
The prophet Zechariah saw me in filthy garments, with Satan standing to accuse me, until an angel had me reclothed in clean robes.
Together with the governor Zerubbabel, I rebuilt the altar and began the temple.
I share my name with the military leader who led Israel into the land centuries before me.

question: Which mocking official am I?
reference: Nehemiah 2; 4; 6; 13 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Tobiah No. 2')

clues: I was called the Ammonite servant, and I opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall.
I sneered that if even a fox climbed on their wall, it would break down their stonework.
I was tied by marriage to many nobles of Judah, who kept praising me to the governor.
While the governor was away, a priest gave me a room in the temple courtyard, and on his return he threw my furniture out.

question: Which replacement apostle am I?
reference: Acts 1:15-26 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Matthias')

clues: I had been with Jesus from his baptism until the day he was taken up.
After Judas fell away, the remaining eleven wanted a twelfth witness of the resurrection.
Two men were put forward, and the disciples prayed and cast lots.
The lot fell on me, and I was numbered with the eleven apostles.

question: Which traveler to Emmaus am I?
reference: Luke 24:13-35 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Cleopas')

clues: I was walking with a companion to a village about seven miles from Jerusalem, three days after the crucifixion.
A stranger caught up with us and asked what we were discussing so sadly.
We told him we had hoped the man who was crucified would be the one to set Israel free.
Our hearts burned as he explained the Scriptures, and we recognized him only when he broke the bread.

question: Which woman who supported Jesus am I?
reference: Luke 8:1-3; 24:10 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Joanna')

clues: My husband, Chuza, was a man over the household of Herod Antipas.
I was one of several women who traveled with Jesus and supported the group out of our own belongings.
Jesus had cured me of an illness.
I was among the women who found the empty tomb and told the apostles, who thought it was nonsense.

question: Which ambitious mother am I?
reference: Matthew 20:20-24; 27:56; Mark 16:1 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Salome No. 1')

clues: Two of my sons were fishermen who left their nets to follow Jesus.
I once knelt before him and asked that they sit at his right and left in his kingdom.
The other ten apostles were indignant with my sons over the request.
I stood watching the crucifixion, and came to the tomb with spices.

question: Which synagogue leader am I?
reference: Mark 5:22-43 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jairus')

clues: I was a presiding officer of the synagogue, and I fell at Jesus' feet begging him to come.
My twelve-year-old daughter was dying.
On the way, a sick woman touched Jesus and there was a delay, and then word came that my girl had died.
Jesus told me not to fear, took her by the hand, and said, "Little girl, get up."

question: Which servant whose ear was healed am I?
reference: John 18:10; Luke 22:50-51 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Malchus')

clues: I was a slave of the high priest.
I was part of the crowd that came with torches and clubs to arrest Jesus at night.
An impulsive disciple drew a sword and cut off my right ear.
Jesus touched the place, healed it, and told the disciple to put the sword away.

question: Which feast am I?
reference: Exodus 12; Luke 22 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Passover')

clues: I am kept on the fourteenth day of the first month, toward evening.
A year-old male lamb without defect is roasted whole and eaten with bitter greens and unleavened bread.
I recall the night the destroyer passed over the houses in Egypt marked with blood.
Jesus instituted a new observance on this very night.

question: Which festival am I?
reference: Leviticus 23:33-43; John 7 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Festival of Booths')

clues: I begin on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and last seven days, with a solemn assembly on the eighth.
The people live in temporary shelters made of leafy branches.
I mark the final ingathering of the harvest and recall the wilderness journey.
It was during me that Jesus stood up and called out about rivers of living water.

question: Which plague of Egypt am I?
reference: Exodus 11-12 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Plague')

clues: I was the last and most terrible of ten blows against Egypt.
At midnight, from Pharaoh's palace to the prisoner's dungeon, the firstborn of every household died.
Israel was spared by marking their doorframes with the blood of a lamb.
That same night, Pharaoh finally drove the people out of his land.

question: Which sacred object am I?
reference: Exodus 25; 37; Joshua 3; 1 Samuel 5 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Ark of the Covenant')

clues: I was a chest of acacia wood covered with gold, with a solid gold lid and two cherubim.
I held the two stone tablets, and for a time a jar of manna and a budded rod.
The Levites carried me on poles, and I led Israel across the Jordan on dry ground.
The Philistines captured me once, and plagues broke out wherever they set me down.

question: Which staff am I?
reference: Numbers 17 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Aaron's Rod')

clues: I was one of twelve staffs, one per tribal chief, laid before God overnight to settle a dispute.
By morning only I had sprouted, blossomed, and produced ripe almonds.
I was kept in front of the ark as a warning sign against rebels.
I proved that God had chosen the tribe of Levi for the priesthood.

question: Which tribe am I?
reference: Numbers 18; Joshua 21 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Levites')

clues: I received no block of territory of my own when Canaan was divided.
Instead I was given forty-eight towns scattered among the other tribes.
My descendants served at the sanctuary, and only one of my families could provide priests.
God told me that he himself was my inheritance.

question: Which lookout mountain am I?
reference: Deuteronomy 34 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Nebo, Mount')

clues: I rise east of the Jordan, directly across from Jericho.
From my summit a 120-year-old leader was shown the whole land he would never enter.
He died on me, and God buried him in a nearby valley.
To this day no one knows the exact place of his grave.

question: Which garden am I?
reference: Matthew 26:36-50; John 18:1 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Gethsemane')

clues: My name means "oil press," and I lay among olive trees on a slope east of Jerusalem.
Jesus often came here with his disciples.
On his last night he prayed here so intensely that his sweat became like drops of blood.
Here Judas arrived with a crowd and identified him with a kiss.
